text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

RTZ-CRA will soon become the first target of "multinational unionism" in the mining industry after Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union president John Maitland convinced the International Federation of Chemical, Energy, Mine and General Workers Unions (ICEM) to use its tactics of "cyberpickets", international comparative wage campaigns, world-wide union networks and globally coordinated industrial action against the mining giant. The ACTU will today meet with one of the architects of the new Internet strategy, ICEM general secretary Vic Thorpe. Page 1.

New Zealand's National Party has secured a deal which will give it a third term of office and see New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters take the position of Treasurer with the power to write the Budget. The deal also included changes to the nation's Reserve Bank Act, widening its target range for underlying inflation from between zero and two per cent to between zero and three per cent and unspecified action to lower the high NZ dollar and to force down high real interest rates. Page 1.

According to the December quarter Westpac-Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry survey of manufacturing firms, the net balance of seven per cent of companies had a decline in new orders, a slight improvement from the September quarter which saw the net balance of firms with a decline in orders reach 15 per cent. Page 3.

A strong return to profitability by National Mutual Life has given National Mutual Holdings a better-than-expected A$210 million maiden profit as a publicly listed company, compared to the prospectus forecast of A$198 million. National Mutual Life reported a A$160.5 million profit in the year to September 30, a turnaround from a A$26.2 million loss in 1995. Page 21.

In its first annual report released yesterday, EnergyAustralia confirmed its position as the leader in the increasingly competitive New South Wales electricity market, announcing a net profit of A$21.8 million on total electricity sales of A$1.08 billion n the four months to June. Page 22.

The Australian Steel Company Pty Ltd chairman Graham Smorgon confirmed yesterday that the Smorgon family had no intention of selling its steel-making operations until after it has consolidated the various parts of the group into a single entity. Smorgon said the company had invested substantial capital to upgrade the mill and would continue to do just that. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett added momentum to the deregulation of the national energy market yesterday by unveiling plans for the sale of State-owned gas and electricity assets, including plans to break State-owned gas utility Gascor up into three distribution businesses and its retail arm into two to five businesses, in a move expected to reap more than A$10 billion. Page 39.

Peter Bartels, whose resignation as Coles Myer managing director is effective from January 1, said last night it was unlikely he would seek employment as a full-time executive again, saying he would take a two or three month break before possibly taking up a project or consultancy position, either locally or overseas. Page 39.

Underpinned by an improved performance in its life insurance division, newly listed National Mutual Holdings Ltd - Australia's number two life insurer - yesterday posted a maiden A$210.9 million profit for the September 30 year, up A$12.9 million on the group's prospectus forecast of A$198 million. Page 39.

A letter to Ansett Australia's 13,000 employees from the airline's present executive chairman Ken Cowley has revealed chief operating officer Hugh Thorburn, who took over Ansett nine months ago after a management split, is resigning to make way for the copany's new executive chairman Rod Eddington. Page 39.

MIM Holdings Ltd's announcement yesterday that it had proven a preliminary resource of about one million ounces of gold from the Mount Wright prospect at its Ravenswood operations in north Queensland could lead to the expansion of the medium-sized operation which currently produces 110,000 ounces of gold a year. Page 41.

Speaking after the official opening of Australia's cleanest combined-cycle co-generation electricity plant at the BP refinery at Kwinana, the chief executive of US-based Edison Mission Energy, Ed Muller, said yesterday that the group was interested in buying the yet-to-be-completed Collie power station in Western Australia, as part of an overall strategy to diversify energy assets outside the United States. Page 41.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Broadcasting Authority is planning to interview Canadian media mogul Izzy Asper when Asper arrives in Australia on Monday and Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston is scheduled to see him on Wednesday over the recent A$105 million purchase of Ten shares by his company CanWest Global Communications. Page 29.

In its first result as a listed company yesterday, National Mutual Holdings posted a A$210.9 million maiden profit, which was 6.5 per cent ahead of the forecasts National Mutual made in the share offer document for its float and more than 82 per cent ahead of last year's result. Page 29.

Giant Australian retailer Coles Myer's shares rose five cents, or 1.1 per cent yesterday, keeping pace with the market at large, in a subdued response to the appointment of Dennis Eck as managing director, reflecting the fact that the market had anticipated the departure of the outgoing CEO Peter Bartels. Page 29.

In a prospectus released yesterday, technology design group Coms 21 revealed it had secured lucrative option deals as part of a sharemarket float that will see the group issuing 18 million shares at 55 cents each, representing 20.2 per cent of the company in an effort to raise A$9.9 million in fresh capital. Page 31.

After the departure of two key executives - general manager Geoffrey Ainsworth and general counsel Richard Wilcock - in the past week, Aristocrat Leisure's woes continued yesterday when the company's shares plunged to their lowest price of A$3.05 before recovering to finish steady at A$3.15 due to investor concern at the changes to the gaming machine manufacturer's board. Page 31.

According to the latest joint Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Westpac survey of industrial trends, unemployment queues are expected to lengthen in the first months of next year, despite business confidence remaining high. The survey showed inflationary pressures remained under control, strengthening the case for a cut in interest rates. Page 31.
THE AGE

National Mutual Holdings unleashed a A$210.9 million maiden profit as a listed company for the year to September yesterday - a result 6.5 per cent ahead of the forecasts in the share offer document in September - at the same time signalling a name change that could see the end of a 127-year history for the National Mutual brand. Page C1.

In a submission to the Wallis Inquiry, Insurance and Superannuation Commission commissioner George Pooley has attacked a proposal by Treasury to dump prudential regulation of superannuation funds and life insurers, claiming that any winding down of regulation would put the financial security of policy holders and members at risk. Page C1.

New Coles Myer managing director Dennis Eck will be charged with the task of running the supermarkets, discount stores and department stores group as a single machine, a task that was only begun in earnest last year, a decade after the group was born. Coles' share price gained five cents yesterday to keep pace with the market - a subdued response to Eck's appointment. Page C1.

First-pass drilling programs by Grenfell Resources and the Minotaur Gold/Lakes Oil partnership have yielded more promising gold results from South Australia's highly-rated Gawler Craton. Grenfell reported widespread low-order gold values in a leached zone at the Mulgathing prospect and scattered low-order gold values at the Boomerang prospect, while the partnership reported shallow drilling had found a series of significant bedrock gold anomalies within an area of 1.2x1 kilometres. Page C3.

Speculation increased yesterday that Newcrest Mining would become the target of a North American gold company after its share price reached a five-month high of A$5.11, but Newcrest believes the interest in its shares simply reflects a return of institutional buying. Page C3.

Launching the Minerals Council of Australia Code for Environmental Management yesterday, Environment Minister Robert Hill said many of Australia's largest mining companies were exceeding the environmental safety standards set by the Government. The new code is part of a push by the mining industry to boost its green image and will see companies voluntarily open their operations to environmental audits. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
